- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 72.5), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (≥0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed or weak (≤0.33) and recent price action is volatile; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling (bullish sentiment with bearish price action), model tends to ignore trend reversal; reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with sentiment divergence.
